Hi @samo25,

Can you describe, in English instead of in a text file, the bug you're trying to fix? Please describe in detail what is wrong with the current text, and how it's caused confusion for web developers or browser implementers. Then describe briefly how you would fix it, and what the possible alternative fixes are.

It's important to understand that you cannot expect us to read through a 4 MB text file to discern what you are trying to accomplish. Instead, please describe it to us in words.

So far from the brief description you've given, what I understand is that some sentences (how many?) use a way of making comparisons that you don't like (could you give an example?) and so instead you want to change it to use something called a "change comparative form" (could you give an example of the new form?). In general this sounds unlikely to be worthwhile, as you haven't identified anyone confused by the current text, but perhaps you simply need to explain in more detail why your phrasing is better and what real-world problem it solves.

For more information on how to contribute to a WHATWG Standard, see the FAQ: https://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/FAQ

OK. I don't think that's a valuable change for this project, @samo25. "more subtle" is a fine way for us to express ourselves.

I'd suggest that if you want to contribute, you focus on technical contributions, not grammatical ones. Or if you insist on focusing on grammatical issues, please make sure they are actual mistakes, not style choices where you prefer one way.

I'll close this, since it sounds like there is no actual issue with the spec causing confusion for web developers or implementers. But I'm happy to continue discussing this with you in the closed thread.

If you only intended to change "more subtle" how did you end up with such a massive patch? Only three lines or so need to change for that. It might be worth learning a bit about Git/GitHub and how that works. Happy to help with any questions on IRC.
